output.brief: The rejections came from a data error in our own system. When the new documentation suite (Tallis) was set up on 1 Aug, the mandarin product record was copied from avocados and kept the avocado carriage temperature of 7.0°C. Our specification for mandarins is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through Tallis (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was instructed at 7.0°C, and the units held 7.0°C. All five were rejected. Every container at 4.0°C passed. This includes Coastway containers and K1 on Meridane, which used the old email booking. It also includes K5 and K7, which used the new fungicide, so the fungicide is not the cause. Meridane ran to the setpoint we gave it, so a claim against them would fail. Lower Serra fruit was somewhat worse within the failed containers, but that is a minor effect and no reason to suspend growers or withhold their pay. Next steps: immediately correct the temperature in the mandarin product record. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check of reefer settings against the product specification before submission. Keep the fungicide supplier as is. Hold off on the claim and the suspension. I am highly confident in this diagnosis.
